18.content: The Pitch In API SDK provides access to the Pitch In API REST APIs.

19.content: Neighbourhood bounties paid through PayPal only when the fix is verified, and again when it lasts. Pledges are PayPal authorizations (held, not charged). The doer is paid with PayPal Payouts. Sign in by sending a sample neighbour id in the X-Pitch-In-User header (demo only; production would use Log in with PayPal).

20.content: Add the SDK to your project from its folder, with whichever package manager your project uses. Give each tool a path containing a slash, such as `../pitch-in-api` — a bare folder name is looked up on PyPI instead, and resolves to whatever project holds that name there:

21.content: Construct `PitchInApiClient` with keyword arguments, and call `close()` when you are done. Every argument is optional.

22.content: Alternatively, scope it — `with PitchInApiClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

23.content: `AsyncPitchInApiClient` mirrors `PitchInApiClient` with **identical method names**, and every endpoint method is a coroutine. It takes the same arguments, with some differences — for example, the transport argument is `custom_async_http_client`.

24.content: Alternatively, scope it — `async with AsyncPitchInApiClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

33.content: The SDK compiles to `dist/` before it can be referenced — run its `build` script once in the SDK folder, then add it to your project by path:

34.content: Create one client and reuse it. Configure its behaviour through `ClientOptions`.

35.content: Nothing in `ClientOptions` is required — `new PitchInApiClient()` compiles — and each option left out falls back to its default. `serverEnvironment` is spelled out above so the environment a call reaches is visible where the client is built rather than inherited silently.

36.content: The package ships both dialects from a single entry, so `require` works with full types. In a TypeScript CommonJS file use the `import ... = require(...)` form — a plain destructuring `require` runs fine but gives you `any`.
